transcript: If I had not pooped in three days, here is exactly what I would do to get things moving today and to make sure it does not keep happening. First, I would warm a glass of prune juice, not cold from the fridge, warm like tea. The body listens better to warmth. Prunes help bring water into the gut, and the warmth tells the body it is time to wake up. If nothing moved by afternoon, I would lie down and massage my belly. Slow, firm circles. Start low on the right side. Move up, across under the ribs, then down the left. That is the path everything travels inside you. But listen carefully. The real question is not only how to go today, the real question is why does this keep happening. When the body is healthy, it knows how to let go. But today, many people are holding inside what should have left days ago. And most of the time, the body is missing one simple thing, soluble fiber. Without enough of it, everything inside moves too slowly. The body pulls the water back. Things dry up, harden, and going to the bathroom feels like passing a brick. But when your body gets enough soluble fiber, it turns into a soft gel that helps hold water and keeps things soft, so the body can move it out the way it was meant to. This is not about forcing the body, it is about helping the body remember what it already knows. The one I trust is physicians choice. Two clean ingredients, soluble corn and gar fiber, nothing else. It dissolves smoothly in any drink, even morning coffee. Search PC fiber on Amazon or check the link in my profile. And if you have strong pain, vomiting, or bleeding, talk to a doctor.
